title: Public decoder side-data profile

decision.finding: The private public-Decoder path retains a duplicate side-data scratch view. The profile proves at least 2,286,976 B of duplicate directly allocated typed slices per p720 NewDecoder; arena-backed CDEF and restoration-boundary portions are additional.
decision.speed_evidence: The p720 warm profile attributed about 0.9% of sampled CPU to side-data bind/attach scopes combined; the constructor scratch function had no CPU-profile samples.
decision.disposition: Do not implement this as a speed improvement without a matched whole-operation A/B that demonstrates a gain. No speedup is claimed here.

go_binary.build_provenance: At build time only internal/av1/motion/subpel_probe_test.go was dirty and restored by overlay. Production sources matched HEAD at ff357374. Subsequent candidate source edits occurred after the immutable benchmark binary was frozen and cannot affect these profiling runs.

benchmark_boundaries.cold_fresh_decoder: Timed benchmark operation: NewDecoderFromIVF over preloaded IVF bytes (including IVF parse and packet-payload copies), drain all DecodeNext results, observe frame dimensions and first/last visible byte of Y/U/V, then Close. Corpus load and one benchmark warmup are outside b.ResetTimer.
benchmark_boundaries.warm_reset_decode: Construct and warm one decoder before timing. Timed operation: Reset, drain DecodeNext, observe frame dimensions and first/last visible byte of Y/U/V. Close is benchmark cleanup outside the timer.
benchmark_boundaries.profile_scope: CPU profile collection spans process and benchmark setup/warmup as well as timed iterations, even where b.ResetTimer excludes setup from ns/op. Allocation profiles are process-cumulative; do not treat their total as per-iteration bytes.
benchmark_boundaries.correctness_scope: These profile invocations used -test.run '^$'; the benchmark checked the 48-frame count and consumed output-edge observations, but did not compute MD5 during profiling.

source_proof.fact: newDecoderStreamScratch allocates Event through newDecoderEventScratch, which allocates one DecoderFrameWorkSideDataScratch, and also allocates a second stream SideData backing of the planned shape. Both views allocate LoopFilterMap, LoopFilterMasks, LoopFilterLevelCache, and RestorationRecords.
decoderArenaSize.addStream adds the nested event side-data arena and a second stream side-data arena, matching the two scratch views.

The initial event bind returns a side-data view, but NewDecoder ignores that return. The event runner stores runtime.SideData (&d.sideData), and later per-event binds use the stream runner's SideDataScratch. The event scratch backing therefore remains retained in d.scratch after its initial binding.

LayeredDecoder also uses the scratch helper and stream SideData view; any future private alias optimization needs layered ownership/error tests. Caller-owned low-level scratch APIs should retain their semantics.

The per-frame high-level path binds/clears side data, then attaches it to the batch residual runner and FrameWorkState. Those attachment setters reset CDEF/LF/restoration data again. Keep public Bind/Set validation and malformed/split-tile semantics; no reset skip was inferred for untested coverage conditions.

source_size_ledger.p720_logical_backing: 320x180 MI shape gives 1,958,400 B of LoopFilterMap records plus 230,400 B of LoopFilterLevelCache per backing, before masks/restoration/CDEF.
source_size_ledger.allocation_profile_note: The exact profile below counts allocator-charged bytes (Go size classes), which differ slightly from requested slice lengths.

refs: src/decode.c:2996-3014 resizes loop-filter mask/level backing only when geometry changes.
src/decode.c:3039 clears the loop-filter mask once per frame.
src/picture.c:71-88 obtains the backing through the picture pool.
src/mem.c:239-272 reuses retired same-size buffers; this does not permit reusing live reference surfaces.
dav1d_reference.scope_note: Reference ownership/design context only; this is not a measured Go-versus-dav1d performance comparison.

p720_cold_alloc_1x.direct_allocation_scope: LoopFilterMap, LoopFilterMasks, LoopFilterLevelCache, and RestorationRecords allocated directly in newDecoderSideDataScratch; arena-backed CDEF maps and restoration boundaries are not included.

p720_cold_alloc_space: Type: alloc_space; total profile bytes: 81,102,064 B.
Source lines: LoopFilterMap 7,864,320 B; LoopFilterMasks 327,680 B; LoopFilterLevelCache 950,272 B; RestorationRecords 5,632 B.

The allocation profile covers benchmark warmup plus one measured cold operation: two Decoder constructions and four calls to newDecoderSideDataScratch. The exact 9,147,904 B divided by four calls is 2,286,976 B of direct typed allocations per scratch view; one equivalent view is the duplicate in this private path. Arena-backed CDEF and restoration-boundary portions are additional.
p720_warm_cpu_side_data: DecoderFrameWorkBatchResidualRunner.SetSideData: 70 ms cumulative (0.46%); LoopFilterMap.Reset 40 ms and RestorationFrameBuffers.ResetRecords 30 ms.
SetDecoderFrameWorkSideData: 20 ms cumulative (0.13%); this overlaps the internal FrameWorkState.SetSideData sample and must not be added twice.
These listed sequential bind/batch/state scopes total about 140 ms, ~0.91% of the sampled CPU; profile resolution is 10 ms and this is not a timing acceptance result.
p720_broad_hot_paths: Cold profile: partitionWalker.walkNode 8.70 s cumulative (55.48% of 15.68 s); prepared postfilter 5.01 s (31.95%); CDEF 2.26 s (14.41%); inter prediction 2.09 s (13.33%).
Warm profile: tile.walkBlocks 9.21 s cumulative (60.00% of 15.35 s); prepared postfilter 4.53 s (29.51%); CDEF 1.93 s (12.57%); inter prediction 2.15 s (14.01%).
Cumulative scopes overlap. The newDecoderSideDataScratch function had no CPU-profile match; no constructor-time speed gain is established.

limitations: This is an attribution profile, not an A/B benchmark or a speedup claim.

The CPU profiles include setup/warmup samples; allocation profiles are process-cumulative. The 100x warm benchmark printed 5,327 B/op with 0 allocs/op, while the separate 1x allocation-profile benchmark printed 0 B/op and 0 allocs/op. Preserve this discrepancy; do not claim a warm-path allocation from it.
The p720 100x benchmark latencies are measured while CPU profiling is active and are not clean timing baselines.
A future scratch alias must preserve public caller-owned Bind/Set behavior and validate both Decoder and LayeredDecoder ownership, reset, malformed-input, and split-tile paths.
No whole-operation speed gain was demonstrated. Under the user's end-to-end speed objective, defer implementation until a paired public-operation A/B shows a repeatable gain.
